An American Airlines commercial aircraft approaches to land at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, as seen from the Lincoln Memorial at the National Mall, Washington, DC, US, on November 2, 2026 [Umit Bektas/Reuters]By ReutersPublished On 13 Nov 202613 Nov 2026
The United States has grounded flights across the country after a “communication issue” impacted traffic control centres, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said.
“FAA [Federal Aviation Administration] technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide immediate updates as we have them,” Duffy wrote on social media.
The FAA said in a post on X that there had been a “temporary telecommunications outage” and that, as a precaution, all flights were being halted. International flights would be handled case by case, it added.
About 7,000 flights have been either delayed or cancelled due to the stop, according to FlightAware.
Some 4,042 flights were in the air, heading to US airports, when the ground stop was ordered, according to the tracking site Flightradar24.
The communication issue affects all 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers, which guide aircraft.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters there was no indication that the ground stop was triggered by a threat to the US. “Everybody’s safe. The flights are accounted for,” he said. “This is not another 9/11.”
President Donald Trump had been briefed, he said.
Asked whether a planned rollout of a new AI tool meant to help air traffic controllers could be to blame, Mullin said officials had not ruled it out. “You just can’t rule out anything at this point. We are going through that process,” he said.

item.title: [CBS News World] Microsoft seeing "continued recovery" amid major worldwide outage
item.description:
From Asia to the U.S., a Microsoft outage involving services like Outlook and Teams lingered into a second day on Friday, impacting users, companies and government operations around the world.
The outage affected a wide range of Microsoft 365 offerings that interact with its Exchange Online and email services. Services including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot were reported by users to be down.
The Redmond, Washington-based company said on Friday that it was making "encouraging recovery progress," noting improvements in email delivery. However, users may still experience "intermittent access issues" or "delayed email delivery" as recovery efforts continue, Microsoft said.
The company also reported "broader improvements" in North America and "sustained improvements across much of Europe," as well as "encouraging recovery signals" in the Asia-Pacific region.
"We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners," Microsoft said Friday on X. "We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously."
While Microsoft appeared to be making headway toward a resolution, the company said Friday afternoon that it did not have an "ETA for full recovery yet."
The outage affected Microsoft's suite of business products, as well as those tailored for personal use by individuals, students and families. Users in more than 70 countries and territories experienced disruptions, according to Downdetector, a website that tracks technology outages.
"Microsoft in a Friday the 13th moment as global outage [causes] a very bad day in Redmond," Yorkville Ives and Co. tech analyst Dan Ives said in an X post Friday. "There will be major questions for MSFT in this global outage."

item.title: [ABC News World] Gold smuggled from war zones entered the UAE despite new regulations, report says
item.description:
Gold smuggled from war zones entered the UAE despite new regulations, report says
A new report says that the United Arab Emirates remains a key destination for gold smuggled from conflict zones despite new regulations on the tradeByHEBA FAROUK MAHFOUZ Associated PressNovember 13, 2026, 12:59 PM
CAIRO -- The United Arab Emirates remains a key destination for gold smuggled from war zones despite new regulations on the trade imposed by the government after facing international pressure, a new report says.
Many gold refiners and traders in the UAE are not following the rules and enforcement is lax, according to the report by Swissaid, a Switzerland-based aid and development group. The report recommended that the UAE be added to an international watchlist for possible financial wrongdoing.
The Emirates, which refines and processes the precious metal to send to major markets like Switzerland, India and China, was the second-biggest gold exporter in the world after Switzerland in 2024, a year after the new rules took effect. Smuggled gold from Russia, Yemen and Sudan continues to flow into the UAE, the report says.
The UAE introduced the new guidelines to regulate the gold trade, including responsible sourcing and vetting supply chains, after a global anti-money laundering body raised concerns that the UAE was not doing enough to stop criminals and militants from hiding wealth there.
Despite the new rules, the UAE imported at least 591 tons of illicit gold, valued at $74 billion, the report says. Gold smuggled out of conflict zones, Russia or African countries accounted for 42% of the UAE's total imports of the precious metal in 2024, the report says.
Imports of the precious metal mined and smuggled out of Africa made up nearly half the gold coming into the UAE from the continent, the report said. Some of that gold entered the UAE officially, through third countries. That trade showed a slight increase in 2024, according to the report.

Trump bought Nvidia stock as he helped chipmaker with change to export rule
President purchased up to $5m of stock before revoking Biden-era rule that limited Nvidia’s ability to sell to China
Donald Trump bought Nvidia stock worth millions of dollars as he made decisions on America’s China policy that would benefit the chipmaker, an analysis has found.
In May 2025, Trump’s administration rescinded a Biden-era rule designed to prevent the most advanced US-made AI chips from being exported to China.
This rule aimed to strengthen the US’s own chip industry and to protect America from what was widely regarded as a national security threat: the possibility that China might develop superior AI.
In the days before he rescinded the rule, Trump’s public financial disclosures indicate that he bought between $1m (£760,000) and $5m worth of Nvidia stock – a purchase noted in an analysis by the anti-corruption group DeKleptocracy.
He also bought shares in other tech companies, including Apple, Meta and Microsoft.

item.description:
Hundreds of roaming cows wreak havoc in North Macedonian town, frustrating farmers
Residents of Kriva Palanka in North Macedonia are dealing with a herd of over 1,000 roaming cattleByKONSTANTIN TESTORIDES Associated PressNovember 13, 2026, 11:17 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
KRIVA PALANKA, North Macedonia -- They descend from the surrounding hills, mostly at night, chomping their way through gardens and crops to satiate their hunger.
For years, residents of Kriva Palanka, a farming town of about 19,000 people in northeastern North Macedonia, have struggled with a herd of roaming cattle that has grown to more than 1,000 animals, destroying property and threatening their livelihood.
It's not just crops. The wandering cows pose a serious risk to the town's water supply and to drivers on a road that leads to neighboring Bulgaria, residents say.
Many fault the country's bureaucratic maze for failing to enforce a 2024 Food and Veterinary Agency order to seize the herd from their three owners.
And even when authorities took legal action against one of the owners, bureaucratic failures derailed the case and allowed the owner to walk free, Kriva Palanka Mayor Sashko Mitovski said.
Mitovski said residents have had enough and are staging protests to urge authorities to take action.
He is asking the conservative government of Prime Minister Hristijan Mickoski to declare a 30-day state of emergency in the municipality for authorities to resolve the bovine problem once and for all.
“The number of cattle has increased from 400 four years ago to more than 1,000 today,” Mitovski told The Associated Press.

Singapore's government confirmed in a statement this week that it reached out to both the U.S. Department of Justice and the FBI for assistance with its investigation.
Alice Huang is the suspected Chinese spy at the center of the extramarital affair scandal that toppled Nvidia founder Jensen Huang from the helm of the global tech giant he built over three decades.

CTI via Reuters TV

Watch: What we know so far about Nvidia CEO resignationByLily Jamali, North America Technology correspondent and Peter Hoskins, Business reporterPublished9 November 2026Updated 12 November 2026
One of the AI industry's most important figures has resigned amid allegations that he had extramarital affairs with two women - one a suspected Chinese spy and the other a company executive.
Chip-maker Nvidia hired a major law firm earlier this week to investigate CEO Jensen Huang's reported relationship with a woman who was allegedly a Chinese intelligence asset.
Now he has resigned after its stocks plummeted on Wednesday following US media reports about a second alleged affair.
Huang admitted, external earlier this week to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and he apologised for hurting her and their children.
Here is what we know about the affair and why it matters.
Nvidia stocks plummet in US after CEO Jensen Huang quits in wake of affair with suspected Chinese spy
How was Huang removed?
Nvidia's board met on Wednesday evening to decide whether its CEO should remain with the company.
It had 11 directors on its board, including Huang. The firm's CEO could be removed with or without cause by a majority vote of directors.
But that wasn't in the end needed - the board instead announced Huang had resigned as president, CEO and board member.
It thanked him for his "immeasurable contributions" to Nvidia, which it said were "profound".
There was no mention of the accusations of adultery.
Who will replace him?
Nvidia Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO.
It is less clear is who will replace Huang on a permanent basis.
One possibility is Nvidia co-founder Chris Malachowsky. He has been at the company as long as Huang, and for years led its product engineering work.

item.description:

View image in fullscreen
‘I am happy to put all this behind me and continue with my writing journey’ … Simbarashe Kundizeza
Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story
After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’
The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation.
Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October.
Five days later, the Atlantic published an article titled “Yet another literary prize winner seems to be AI”, in which the author and journalist Vauhini Vara said the AI-detection software Pangram, which itself uses AI, had deemed the story to be almost completely artificially generated.
The Caine prize chair, Ellah Wakatama, said in a statement: “From our detailed investigation, we feel the evidence is clear: The Blue Fighter was human-written. We now look forward to awarding and celebrating Simbarashe Steyn Kundizeza … before the end of the year.”
She said: “When concerns were raised, we have a duty as an organisation to look at them carefully and fairly,” adding that the prize had taken a “human-centred” approach to its investigation.
“Our review included interviews with the author, the 2026 judging panel and The Shallow Tales Review, where the story was first published,” Wakatama said. “It also included independent and expert-led metadata analysis of drafts written by the author.”

Watch: Chris Cash says counter-terror officers entered his bedroom and arrested himByJoe Pike, politics investigations correspondent and Phil Kemp, politics reporterPublished11 November 2026
A British man who was charged with spying for China has told the BBC he was a "convenient fall guy" for UK police and security services who wanted to put espionage threats by foreign states "on the map".
Chris Cash, a former parliamentary researcher, has shared more than 6,000 messages with us revealing how a Chinese official sought information about sensitive political matters in the UK - including the 2022 Tory leadership battle to decide the next prime minister.
The messages show how Cash's friend in China, Chris Berry - with whom he had been sharing information - dramatically described a "secret" meeting between Berry and a high-ranking Chinese official.
Berry said he had been told that China was concerned about how a British MP it had sanctioned might be promoted to a cabinet role.
The messages also reveal how Cash used his friend as a reference during vetting for a parliamentary pass - which was approved.
Like Cash, Berry was also charged with espionage. The two men consistently maintained their innocence.
In Cash's first interview since his acquittal, which sparked a political row over the government's failure to designate China as a "threat", he says he would "never do anything" to harm UK national security.
But he admits he was "unprofessional and naive" to send "gossiping" texts to his friend, whom he met in 2018 when they both taught English in a school in China.
Although the trove of messages shows him discussing sensitive topics, there is no evidence in them that Cash was paid by, or sympathetic to, the Chinese Communist Party.

item.title: [BBC China] Nvidia hires major US law firm to investigate alleged Chinese spy affair
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has become the face of the US AI boomByKali Hays, Technology reporter and Lily Jamali, North America Technology correspondentPublished10 November 2026
Nvidia has hired one of the largest law firms in the US to investigate the affair between its own chief executive and an alleged Chinese spy.
Jensen Huang, who co-founded the tech company, has admitted to having a romantic relationship outside of his marriage. The woman, Alice Huang, is alleged to be a spy for Beijing.
Nvidia said on Tuesday that it had hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, and that its attorney Joon Kim would lead "a thorough and independent investigation". The FBI is also conducting its own probe.
The company's share price has fallen almost to a yearly low, with $500bn (£375bn) wiped of its stock market value since Friday.
Nvidia is widely considered one of the most important companies behind the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, given it is the sole manufacturer of a computer chip used in AI tools.
It is the world's second most valuable company after Apple and its chips have become a matter of national security for US officials who are keen to win the AI race.
Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, and is not related to Jensen Huang, was an executive at Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has been a customer of Nvidia.
Megaspeed had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia has said was investigated and debunked.
Nvidia has also maintained that the US government did not inform it that Megaspeed posed an intelligence concern.

Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet organisations sending humanitarian aid to the territory.
The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire.
“I think we need to make sure we’re pushing to free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, free Palestine. I think there’s a lot of peace that I’m hoping we get to at some stage,” Hamilton said in October.
A ceasefire agreement reached last year has halted major combat operations in Gaza, but the amount of aid reaching the territory continues to fall far short of the agreed-upon minimum of 600 trucks a day.
Israeli forces have continued to advance, expanding their control from 53% of the territory to at least 60%, an independent commission of UN experts said last month.

item.title: [Guardian World] Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
item.description:
People at the scene of the collision in Giza province. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
People at the scene of the collision in Giza province. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images
Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven
President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo
Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.
An inspection indicated that the Cairo-Aswan train had been stationary on the same track, officials said.
The health ministry gave the casualty toll, adding more than 70 of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment.
Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years the government has announced modernisation initiatives to improve its railways.
Ayman Gamal, a resident of Kafr Girza in al-Ayyat where the crash occurred, said people rushed to the scene, pulled out survivors and called ambulances.
Gamal said he saw about 80 of the injured being taken by ambulances to hospital. Some passengers were trapped inside one of the carriages of the stationary train and died, he said.
View image in fullscreen
People search for survivors after the collision. Photograph: AP
Egypt’s president, Abdel Fatah al-Sisi, said in a social media post that he had ordered a prompt investigation.
